theory.overview: Bit manipulation operates on individual bits of integers using bitwise operators. It's efficient for problems involving binary representation, subsets, flags, and optimization. Common operations: AND (&), OR (|), XOR (^), NOT (~), left shift (<<), right shift (>>). This chapter covers bit operators, common tricks, and bit manipulation problems.

sections.title: Bitwise Operators
sections.content: AND (&): 1 if both bits 1. OR (|): 1 if either bit 1. XOR (^): 1 if bits different. NOT (~): flip all bits. Left shift (<<): multiply by 2^n. Right shift (>>): divide by 2^n (arithmetic preserves sign). These are O(1) operations.

sections.title: Common Bit Tricks
sections.content: Check if odd: n & 1. Check if power of 2: n & (n-1) == 0. Get lowest set bit: n & -n. Clear lowest set bit: n & (n-1). Count set bits: Brian Kernighan's algorithm. Swap without temp: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b.
tricks: Count set bits: n &= n-1 loop

sections.title: Bitmask Applications
sections.content: Subset representation: bitmask where bit i set means element i in subset. Generate all subsets: iterate 0 to 2^n-1. Check if bit set: (mask >> i) & 1. Set bit: mask | (1 << i). Clear bit: mask & ~(1 << i). Toggle bit: mask ^ (1 << i). Used in DP, backtracking, and combinatorial problems.

sections.title: XOR Properties
sections.content: XOR is commutative and associative. a ^ a = 0. a ^ 0 = a. a ^ b ^ a = b (cancels out). Used for finding single element in pairs, swapping without temp, and finding missing number.

sections.title: Bit Manipulation vs Other Approaches
sections.content: Bit manipulation: O(1) per operation, space-efficient, but can be less readable. Hash map: O(1) average, more readable, but uses more space. Array: O(n) operations, simple. Choose bit manipulation for space efficiency and when operations naturally map to bits.

keyConcepts.name: Two's Complement
keyConcepts.description: Representation of signed integers. Negative numbers: ~n + 1. Explains right shift behavior (arithmetic preserves sign).

keyConcepts.name: Lowest Set Bit
keyConcepts.description: Rightmost 1 bit. n & -n isolates it. Useful for Brian Kernighan's algorithm and bitmask operations.

keyConcepts.name: Bitmask
keyConcepts.description: Integer where each bit represents a boolean flag or element presence. Compact representation of subsets.

keyConcepts.name: XOR Cancellation
keyConcepts.description: XORing same value twice cancels out. Used to find single element in pairs (all others appear twice).

steps.title: Identify Bit Operation
steps.description: Determine which bit operation needed (AND, OR, XOR, shift, etc.).

steps.title: Apply Operation
steps.code: result = a & b; or result = a << n;

steps.title: Iterate if Needed
steps.description: For operations on all bits (count set bits, etc.), iterate through bits.

steps.title: Handle Edge Cases
steps.description: Handle negative numbers (two's complement), overflow, and sign extension.

practiceProblems.title: Single Number
practiceProblems.description: Find element that appears once (all others appear twice).
practiceProblems.solution: XOR all elements. Pairs cancel out, single remains.

practiceProblems.title: Single Number II
practiceProblems.description: Find element appearing once (others appear three times).
practiceProblems.solution: Count bits at each position modulo 3. Or use bit manipulation with two variables.

practiceProblems.title: Single Number III
practiceProblems.description: Find two elements appearing once (others appear twice).
practiceProblems.solution: XOR all to get xor of two singles. Find rightmost set bit, partition array, XOR each partition.

practiceProblems.title: Number of 1 Bits
practiceProblems.description: Count set bits in integer.
practiceProblems.solution: Brian Kernighan: n &= n-1 until n=0. Count iterations.

practiceProblems.title: Reverse Bits
practiceProblems.description: Reverse bits of 32-bit unsigned integer.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterate 32 bits. Extract bit from right, add to result at left.
practiceProblems.hints: Extract from right, add to left

practiceProblems.title: Missing Number
practiceProblems.description: Find missing number in [0,n] containing n numbers.
practiceProblems.solution: XOR all numbers with 0 to n. Missing number remains.

practiceProblems.title: Sum of Two Integers
practiceProblems.description: Calculate sum without + or - operators.
practiceProblems.solution: Use XOR for sum without carry, AND << 1 for carry. Repeat until no carry.
practiceProblems.hints: XOR for sum, AND << 1 for carry

practiceProblems.title: Power of Two
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is power of 2.

practiceProblems.title: Power of Four
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is power of 4.
practiceProblems.solution: n > 0, power of 2, and (n-1) % 3 == 0 (only one bit set in odd positions).

practiceProblems.title: Hamming Distance
practiceProblems.description: Number of positions where bits differ between two integers.
practiceProblems.solution: XOR, count set bits.

practiceProblems.title: Total Hamming Distance
practiceProblems.description: Sum of hamming distances between all pairs.
practiceProblems.solution: For each bit position, count ones. Distance contribution = ones * (n-ones).
practiceProblems.hints: Count ones at each bit position

practiceProblems.title: Find the Difference
practiceProblems.description: Find added character in t (t is s shuffled plus one char).
practiceProblems.solution: XOR all characters. Result is extra character.

practiceProblems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
practiceProblems.description: Find maximum XOR of any two numbers in array.
practiceProblems.solution: Bit Trie (32 bits). For each number, find number in Trie that maximizes XOR.
practiceProblems.hints: Bit Trie, maximize XOR bit by bit

practiceProblems.title: Maximum XOR With an Element
practiceProblems.description: For each query, find max XOR with any number ≤ limit.
practiceProblems.solution: Bit Trie. For each query, search Trie respecting limit constraint.

practiceProblems.title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
practiceProblems.description: Bitwise AND of all numbers in range [m, n].
practiceProblems.solution: Find common prefix of m and n. Shift right until equal, shift back.

practiceProblems.title: Gray Code
practiceProblems.description: Generate n-bit Gray code sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: G(i) = i ^ (i >> 1). Or recursive: G(n) = G(n-1) + reverse(G(n-1)) with leading bit.

practiceProblems.title: Complement of Base 10 Integer
practiceProblems.description: Complement of integer (flip bits in binary representation without leading zeros).
practiceProblems.solution: Find number of bits, create mask, XOR with mask.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits
practiceProblems.description: Check if binary representation has alternating bits.
practiceProblems.solution: n ^ (n >> 1) should be all 1s (alternating). Check if n ^ (n >> 1) + 1 is power of 2.

practiceProblems.title: Binary Gap
practiceProblems.description: Maximum distance between consecutive 1s in binary.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterate bits, track last 1 position, update max gap.

practiceProblems.title: Counting Bits
practiceProblems.description: Count set bits for all numbers from 0 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: DP: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1). Or Brian Kernighan for each.

practiceProblems.title: Integer Replacement
practiceProblems.description: Minimum operations to reduce n to 1 (n even: n/2, n odd: n+1 or n-1).
practiceProblems.solution: Bit manipulation or greedy. For odd n, choose n+1 if n is 3 or ends with 01, else n-1.

practiceProblems.title: UTF-8 Validation
practiceProblems.description: Validate UTF-8 encoding.
practiceProblems.solution: Check leading bits to determine byte sequence length. Validate each byte.
practiceProblems.hints: Check leading bits for sequence length

practiceProblems.title: Reordered Power of 2
practiceProblems.description: Check if n is power of 2 after reordering digits.
practiceProblems.solution: Count digits of n. Compare with digit counts of powers of 2 up to 2^29.
practiceProblems.hints: Compare digit counts with powers of 2

practiceProblems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
practiceProblems.description: Find duplicate in array of n+1 integers where each is 1 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: Floyd's cycle detection (treat array as linked list). Or XOR (not for this variant).

practiceProblems.title: Subsets
practiceProblems.description: Generate all subsets using bitmask.
practiceProblems.solution: Iterate mask from 0 to 2^n-1. For each mask, collect elements where bit is set.

minigame.description: Master bit manipulation! XOR, bitmasks, and bit tricks.
